title: Why a cache helps reads (and not writes)

steps.caption: An API and one SQL database. 1k rps, 90% reads: the database is barely busy.
10k rps. The database can do 5k: it saturates first.
Add a cache with a 90% hit ratio. 90% of reads never reach the database: it now sees 0.9k reads + 1k writes.
Flip to write-heavy: 30% reads. Every write still goes to the database (7k/s). The cache can't help writes.
Back to 90% reads, at 20k rps. With write-through, writes update the cache, so the hit ratio stays at 90%. The database sees 1.8k reads + 2k writes.
Switch the cache to invalidate-on-write: every write evicts its key, so the next read misses. In this model the hit ratio falls to about 81% and the database tips over.
